title: Mohd Abdul Samad v. State of Telangana & Anr.

legal_context.subject: Maintenance rights of a divorced Muslim woman
legal_context.important_note: The Supreme Court considered whether a divorced Muslim woman can seek maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and addressed the relationship between that remedy and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.

case_summary.issue: Whether a divorced Muslim woman can claim maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
case_summary.holding: A divorced Muslim woman can seek maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The Supreme Court held that the remedy under Section 125 is available to a divorced Muslim woman and is not excluded merely because she is governed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986.
important_principles: A divorced Muslim woman can invoke the maintenance remedy under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
The remedy under Section 125 CrPC is a secular remedy and is not confined by the personal law of the parties.
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 does not take away the remedy available to a divorced Muslim woman under Section 125 CrPC.
The availability of a remedy under the 1986 Act does not by itself prevent a divorced Muslim woman from seeking maintenance under Section 125 CrPC.
The judgment emphasizes the protective purpose of maintenance provisions and the need to prevent destitution and vagrancy.
